targetAudience.primary: Architects of multi-agent context, subagent delegation and policy governance
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands developer-role instructions, context inheritance and agent forks.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Child-specific control text can lose provenance, leak into the parent or be duplicated, while a developer label can be mistaken for proof that its source was authorized.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change adds a typed DeveloperInstructions fragment and verifies a child-only instruction is excluded from the parent and represented once in the demonstrated full-history child request.

externalHook.description: A typed label can identify where an instruction belongs without proving who was permitted to create it.

coreProposition: Forked-agent contexts need two separate control planes: typed lineage must preserve whether instructions are inherited, replaced or child-local across derivation, while independent authority records must identify the principal, policy source and scope that permit those instructions.

originalValue.description: Separates context derivation from permission, using the demonstrated child-only boundary to define non-leakage, single representation and re-authorization requirements across fork, compaction, resume and replay.

readerTakeaway: Carry typed origin and scope with each instruction fragment, test parent exclusion and child representation at request boundaries, and never treat developer-role provenance as an authorization credential.

supported: Developer instructions receive explicit developer role and generic.developer_instructions content kind.
Full-history fork logic conditionally injects child-only guidance when preserved context would omit it.
The regression verifies parent exclusion and one child occurrence.
unsupported: Authenticated authority to set child instructions
Coverage of every history and compaction mode
uncertain: How competing typed instruction fragments should be ordered
How lineage survives every compaction and resume path

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general multi-agent context and authority architecture without first-party project dependence.

decisionReason: The implementation provides a concrete fork boundary and supports an independently useful two-plane governance model with explicit limits.
